methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: AI Ready Roanoke evaluates use for new technology in Roanoke Valley - Roanoke Times
signals.signal_reading: AI Ready Roanoke represents intentional community-led capacity building in a mid-sized metro outside traditional tech hubs, signaling potential for distributed deep capability if evaluation translates into implementation and peer learning networks.

signals.title: Warner, Anthropic launch AI pilot to help Hampton Roads military families find local resources - The Legacy Newspaper
signals.signal_reading: Platform-delivered AI pilot (Anthropic) for military families demonstrates shallow, broad adoption pattern where sophisticated external tools serve specific use cases without building local AI development capacity or transferable technical skills.

signals.title: VCU partners with the Better Business Bureau to bring AI support to Central Virginia businesses - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU-BBB partnership concentrates AI expertise delivery through established institutions to serve Central Virginia businesses, reinforcing Richmond's role as a secondary hub but requiring business adoption rather than building distributed grassroots capability.

signals.title: AI is already common in Virginia Beach high schools. Leaders weigh guardrails - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: AI already common in Virginia Beach schools yet leaders still weighing guardrails signals reactive shallow adoption without strategic depth—students use tools without districts building systematic AI literacy or workforce preparation infrastructure.

signals.title: Problems with AI use in Roanoke County schools: It’s not the students - WFIR News
signals.signal_reading: Problems with AI use in Roanoke County schools stem from educators rather than students, revealing implementation without adequate professional development—technology adoption outpacing institutional capacity building creates shallow, problematic deployment.
